newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end flat, tone cautious on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end flat, tone cautious on rupiah.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended flat in slow trading on Tuesday, with newly-listed counters staging modest debuts despite cautious sentiment because of the weak rupiah, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index ended 0.96 points, or 0.13 percent, lower at 711.44 points.
Decliners led advancers by 68 to 63 with 57 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 390 billion rupiah compared with around 567 billion rupiah on Monday.
"We hope there would be no more speculative attacks on the rupiah later today or tommorow so that players would re-enter the market and do some bargain-hunting," one broker said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,573.00 at 0945 GMT against an opening of 2,633/43 after recording its largest-ever single-day loss on Monday due to overseas speculative attacks.
Brokers said the market focus was on newly-listed textile firm Panasia Filament and Lippo General Insurance .
Lippo General Insurance was the most active, with some 26 million shares traded. It was last traded at 2,700 rupiah against an initial offer price of 2,225 rupiah.
Panasia Filament was also active and was last traded at 750 rupiah against an initial offer price of 650 rupiah.

The stock exchange suspended trading in small-sized plastics manufacturer PT Langgeng Makmur Plastic Industry just before the close on Tuesday after a sharp rise in the firm's stock, an exchange official said.

Langgeng Makmur was up 325 rupiah, or 31.71 percent, at 1,350 rupiah in thin trading, with only 72,500 shares traded before it was suspended at around 0850 GMT, ten minutes before the end of trading, the official said.

Brokers said they praised the exchange's move, but said the exchange should get tougher and get into details such as finding out who were behind the sharp rise and their motives so as to prevent recurrences.
They said similar sharp rises had occurred frequently in the stocks of other small-sized firms recently.
Last week, the exchange temporarily suspended trading in shares of animal feed producer CP Prima.
In June, the exchange temporarily suspended footwear manufacturer Super Mitory, electronics firm Jeewon and finance firm Clipan, brokers said.
